sanskrit: bhartā nāma paraṃ nāryā bhūṣaṇaṃ bhūṣaṇair vinā eṣā virahitā tena śobhanāpi na śobhate
english: A husband is indeed the supreme ornament of a woman, beyond all other ornaments. Separated from him, even one who is beautiful does not shine.

sanskrit: duṣkaraṃ kurute 'tyarthaṃ hīno yad anayā nalaḥ dhārayaty ātmano dehaṃ na śokenāvasīdati
english: Nala performs a deed most difficult to bear — deprived of her, he still sustains his own body and does not sink under grief.

sanskrit: imām asitakeśāntāṃ śatapatrāyatekṣaṇām sukhārhāṃ duḥkhitāṃ dṛṣṭvā mamāpi vyathate manaḥ
english: Seeing her, with dark-tipped hair and eyes as wide as lotus petals, she who deserves happiness yet is plunged in sorrow — even my own heart is pained.

sanskrit: kadā nu khalu duḥkhasya pāraṃ yāsyati vai śubhā bhartuḥ samāgamāt sādhvī rohiṇī śaśino yathā
english: When shall this auspicious and chaste woman reach the far shore of her sorrow through reunion with her husband, even as Rohiṇī is reunited with the moon?

sanskrit: asyā nūnaṃ punar lābhān naiṣadhaḥ prītim eṣyati rājā rājyaparibhraṣṭaḥ punar labdhveva medinīm
english: Surely, upon winning her back, the king of Niṣadha will rejoice, like a king fallen from his kingdom who has recovered his realm.

sanskrit: tulyaśīlavayoyuktāṃ tulyābhijanasaṃyutām naiṣadho 'rhati vaidarbhīṃ taṃ ceyam asitekṣaṇā
english: The lord of Niṣadha deserves the daughter of Vidarbha, who matches him in character, age, and lineage — and she, dark-eyed one, deserves him in return.

sanskrit: yuktaṃ tasyāprameyasya vīryasattvavato mayā samāśvāsayituṃ bhāryāṃ patidarśanalālasām
english: It is fitting that I comfort the wife of that immeasurable hero endowed with valor and steadfastness — she who longs to behold her husband.

sanskrit: ayam āśvāsayāmy enāṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanām adṛṣṭapūrvāṃ duḥkhasya duḥkhārtāṃ dhyānatatparām
english: I shall now comfort her — she whose face resembles the full moon, who has never before known such sorrow, who is afflicted with grief and absorbed in brooding.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca evaṃ vimṛśya vividhaiḥ kāraṇair lakṣaṇaiś ca tām upagamya tato bhaimīṃ sudevo brāhmaṇo 'bravīt
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Having thus deliberated by various reasons and identifying marks, the brahmin Sudeva then approached the daughter of Bhīma and spoke.

sanskrit: ahaṃ sudevo vaidarbhi bhrātus te dayitaḥ sakhā bhīmasya vacanād rājñas tvām anveṣṭum ihāgataḥ
english: I am Sudeva, O daughter of Vidarbha, the beloved friend of your brother; by the command of King Bhīma I have come here to search for you.

sanskrit: kuśalī te pitā rājñi janitrī bhrātaraś ca te āyuṣmantau kuśalinau tatrasthau dārakau ca te tvatkṛte bandhuvargāś ca gatasattvā ivāsate
english: Your father the king is well, O queen, and your mother and brothers; your two children are there in good health and long-lived; but all your kinsmen, on your account, live as if bereft of vitality.

sanskrit: abhijñāya sudevaṃ tu damayantī yudhiṣṭhira paryapṛcchat tataḥ sarvān krameṇa suhṛdaḥ svakān
english: Recognizing Sudeva, Damayantī, O Yudhiṣṭhira, then inquired after all her own dear friends and kinsmen one by one.

sanskrit: ruroda ca bhṛśaṃ rājan vaidarbhī śokakarśitā dṛṣṭvā sudevaṃ sahasā bhrātur iṣṭaṃ dvijottamam
english: The daughter of Vidarbha, emaciated by sorrow, wept bitterly, O king, upon suddenly seeing Sudeva, the best of brahmins and beloved friend of her brother.

sanskrit: tato rudantīṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sunandā śokakarśitām sudevena sahaikānte kathayantīṃ ca bhārata
english: Then Sunandā, seeing her weeping and wasted with grief, and speaking privately with Sudeva, O descendant of Bharata —

sanskrit: janitryai preṣayām āsa sairandhrī rudate bhṛśam brāhmaṇena samāgamya tāṃ veda yadi manyase
english: — sent word to the queen-mother: "The handmaid is weeping greatly upon meeting a brahmin; if you think fit, go know who she is."

sanskrit: atha cedipater mātā rājñaś cāntaḥpurāt tadā jagāma yatra sā bālā brāhmaṇena sahābhavat
english: Then the mother of the king of Cedi came forth from the inner apartments to the place where that young woman was together with the brahmin.

sanskrit: tataḥ sudevam ānāyya rājamātā viśāṃ pate papraccha bhāryā kasyeyaṃ sutā vā kasya bhāminī
english: The queen-mother then summoned Sudeva and questioned him, O lord of people: "Whose wife is this woman, or whose daughter, O spirited one?"

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca naṣṭā jñātibhyo bhartur vā vāmalocanā tvayā ca viditā vipra katham evaṃgatā satī
english: "How did this lovely-eyed one come to be lost from her kinsmen or her husband? And how did you, O brahmin, come to know her, and how did she fall into this condition?"

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ tvatto jñātuṃ sarvam aśeṣataḥ tattvena hi mamācakṣva pṛcchantyā devarūpiṇīm
english: "All this I wish to know from you without remainder; tell me truly, for one who is asking, of her who has the beauty of a goddess."

sanskrit: evam uktas tayā rājan sudevo dvijasattamaḥ sukhopaviṣṭa ācaṣṭa damayantyā yathātatham
english: Thus addressed by her, O king, Sudeva the best of twice-born, having seated himself at ease, described Damayantī's story exactly as it was.

sanskrit: sudeva uvāca vidarbharājo dharmātmā bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ suteyaṃ tasya kalyāṇī damayantīti viśrutā
english: Sudeva said: The king of Vidarbha, Bhīma, is righteous-souled and of terrible prowess. This auspicious woman is his daughter, renowned as Damayantī.

sanskrit: rājā tu naiṣadho nāma vīrasenasuto nalaḥ bhāryeyaṃ tasya kalyāṇī puṇyaślokasya dhīmataḥ
english: The king of Niṣadha, Nala by name, son of Vīrasena — this auspicious woman is the wife of that wise and celebrated lord.

sanskrit: sa vai dyūte jito bhrātrā hṛtarājyo mahīpatiḥ damayantyā gataḥ sārdhaṃ na prajñāyata karhi cit
english: That lord of the earth was defeated at dice by his brother, stripped of his kingdom; he departed together with Damayantī and was not found anywhere thereafter.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ damayantyarthe carāmaḥ pṛthivīm imām seyam āsāditā bālā tava putraniveśane
english: We wander this earth in search of Damayantī; and this young woman has been found in the dwelling of your son.

sanskrit: asyā rūpeṇa sadṛśī mānuṣī neha vidyate asyāś caiva bhruvor madhye sahajaḥ piplur uttamaḥ śyāmāyāḥ padmasaṃkāśo lakṣito 'ntarhito mayā
english: No mortal woman here equals her in beauty. Between her brows she bears a congenital mole, a mark of excellence — on that dark-complexioned one it resembles a lotus; I spied it though it was concealed.

sanskrit: malena saṃvṛto hy asyās tanvabhreṇeva candramāḥ cihnabhūto vibhūtyartham ayaṃ dhātrā vinirmitaḥ
english: Covered by grime, it is like the moon veiled by a thin cloud. This mark was fashioned by the Creator as a sign for the sake of her glory.

sanskrit: pratipatkaluṣevendor lekhā nāti virājate na cāsyā naśyate rūpaṃ vapur malasamācitam asaṃskṛtam api vyaktaṃ bhāti kāñcanasaṃnibham
english: As the crescent of the tarnished moon does not shine forth fully, yet her beauty does not perish; though her body is covered with grime and unadorned, it shines plainly like gold.

sanskrit: anena vapuṣā bālā piplunānena caiva ha lakṣiteyaṃ mayā devī pihito 'gnir ivoṣmaṇā
english: By this form and by this very mole I recognized her, this goddess — as a fire is identified by its heat even when covered.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya sudevasya viśāṃ pate sunandā śodhayām āsa piplupracchādanaṃ malam
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Hearing that speech of Sudeva, O lord of people, Sunandā cleansed away the grime that concealed the mole.

sanskrit: sa malenāpakṛṣṭena piplus tasyā vyarocata damayantyās tadā vyabhre nabhasīva niśākaraḥ
english: With the grime wiped away, the mole of Damayantī shone forth — like the night-maker revealed in a cloudless sky.

sanskrit: pipluṃ dṛṣṭvā sunandā ca rājamātā ca bhārata rudantyau tāṃ pariṣvajya muhūrtam iva tasthatuḥ utsṛjya bāṣpaṃ śanakai rājamātedam abravīt
english: Seeing the mole, Sunandā and the queen-mother, O descendant of Bharata, wept and embraced her and stood still for a moment; then, shedding tears softly, the queen-mother spoke thus:

sanskrit: bhaginyā duhitā me 'si piplunānena sūcitā ahaṃ ca tava mātā ca rājanyasya mahātmanaḥ sute daśārṇādhipateḥ sudāmnaś cārudarśane
english: "You are the daughter of my sister, identified by this mole — both I and your mother are daughters of that high-souled king of the Daśārṇas, of Sudāman, O lovely-faced one."

sanskrit: bhīmasya rājñaḥ sā dattā vīrabāhor ahaṃ punaḥ tvaṃ tu jātā mayā dṛṣṭā daśārṇeṣu pitur gṛhe
english: "She was given to King Bhīma, the mighty-armed, while I went to another; and you I saw as a child born in the house of your father in the Daśārṇa land."

sanskrit: yathaiva te pitur gehaṃ tathedam api bhāmini yathaiva hi mamaiśvaryaṃ damayanti tathā tava
english: "As your father's house is to you, so too is this house, O spirited one; as my sovereignty is mine, Damayantī, so too is it yours."

sanskrit: tāṃ prahṛṣṭena manasā damayantī viśāṃ pate abhivādya mātur bhaginīm idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: With a joyful heart, Damayantī, O lord of people, bowed to her mother's sister and spoke these words:

sanskrit: ajñāyamānāpi satī sukham asmy uṣiteha vai sarvakāmaiḥ suvihitā rakṣyamāṇā sadā tvayā
english: "Even while being unrecognized, I have lived here happily, well provided with all desires and always protected by you."

sanskrit: sukhāt sukhataro vāso bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ciraviproṣitāṃ mātar mām anujñātum arhasi
english: "The dwelling will be even happier than this — of that there is no doubt. But O mother's sister, you must give leave to me who have long been separated from my home."

sanskrit: dārakau ca hi me nītau vasatas tatra bālakau pitrā vihīnau śokārtau mayā caiva kathaṃ nu tau
english: "My two little children are there, living without their father, afflicted with grief and without me as well — how must they be?"

sanskrit: yadi cāpi priyaṃ kiṃ cin mayi kartum ihecchasi vidarbhān yātum icchāmi śīghraṃ me yānam ādiśa
english: "If you wish to do anything dear to me, I desire to go to Vidarbha; appoint a conveyance for me quickly."

sanskrit: bāḍham ity eva tām uktvā hṛṣṭā mātṛṣvasā nṛpa guptāṃ balena mahatā putrasyānumate tataḥ
english: "So be it," said the mother's sister joyfully to her, O king; and then, with the consent of her son, she escorted her under a great guard —

sanskrit: prasthāpayad rājamātā śrīmatā naravāhinā yānena bharataśreṣṭha svannapānaparicchadām
english: — the queen-mother dispatched her in a splendid chariot drawn by men, O best of the Bharata line, furnished with food, drink, and all necessities.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā nacirād eva vidarbhān agamac chubhā tāṃ tu bandhujanaḥ sarvaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ pratyapūjayat
english: Then the auspicious one reached Vidarbha before long; all her kinsmen received and honored her with great joy.

sanskrit: sarvān kuśalino dṛṣṭvā bāndhavān dārakau ca tau mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caiva sarvaṃ caiva sakhījanam
english: Seeing all her kinsmen in good health, and her two children, and her mother and father, and all her circle of friends —

sanskrit: devatāḥ pūjayām āsa brāhmaṇāṃś ca yaśasvinī vidhinā pareṇa kalyāṇī damayantī viśāṃ pate
english: — the glorious and auspicious Damayantī worshipped the gods and the brahmins with the highest rites, O lord of people.

sanskrit: atarpayat sudevaṃ ca gosahasreṇa pārthivaḥ prīto dṛṣṭvaiva tanayāṃ grāmeṇa draviṇena ca
english: The king, overjoyed at the mere sight of his daughter, satisfied Sudeva with a thousand cows and also with a village and riches.

sanskrit: sā vyuṣṭā rajanīṃ tatra pitur veśmani bhāminī viśrāntā mātaraṃ rājann idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: After spending the night rested in her father's house, that spirited woman, O king, spoke these words to her mother:

sanskrit: damayanty uvāca māṃ ced icchasi jīvantīṃ mātaḥ satyaṃ bravīmi te naravīrasya vai tasya nalasyānayane yata
english: Damayantī said: If you wish me to live, mother — I speak truly — then strive for the bringing back of that hero among men, Nala.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca damayantyā tathoktā tu sā devī bhṛśaduḥkhitā bāṣpeṇa pihitā rājan nottaraṃ kiṃ cid abravīt
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Thus addressed by Damayantī, that queen, deeply grieved and choked with tears, O king, spoke not a single word in reply.

sanskrit: tadavasthāṃ tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvam antaḥpuraṃ tadā hāhābhūtam atīvāsīd bhṛśaṃ ca praruroda ha
english: Seeing her in that condition, the entire inner chamber was then thrown into great lamentation and wept bitterly.

sanskrit: tato bhīmaṃ mahārāja bhāryā vacanam abravīt damayantī tava sutā bhartāram anuśocati
english: Then the queen spoke to Bhīma, O great king: "Your daughter Damayantī grieves for her husband."

sanskrit: apakṛṣya ca lajjāṃ māṃ svayam uktavatī nṛpa prayatantu tava preṣyāḥ puṇyaślokasya darśane
english: "And she herself has spoken to me, setting aside her shame, O king: 'Let your servants make effort to find the celebrated Nala.'"

sanskrit: tayā pracodito rājā brāhmaṇān vaśavartinaḥ prāsthāpayad diśaḥ sarvā yatadhvaṃ naladarśane
english: Urged by her, the king dispatched obedient brahmins in all directions: "Seek and find Nala."

sanskrit: tato vidarbhādhipater niyogād brāhmaṇarṣabhāḥ damayantīm atho dṛṣṭvā prasthitāḥ smety athābruvan
english: Then by the command of the lord of Vidarbha, those best of brahmins, having come before Damayantī, said "we set out" and addressed her thus:

sanskrit: atha tān abravīd bhaimī sarvarāṣṭreṣv idaṃ vacaḥ bruvadhvaṃ janasaṃsatsu tatra tatra punaḥ punaḥ
english: The daughter of Bhīma then spoke these words to them: "Proclaim this speech in all kingdoms, in public assemblies here and there, again and again:"

sanskrit: kva nu tvaṃ kitava chittvā vastrārdhaṃ prasthito mama utsṛjya vipine suptām anuraktāṃ priyāṃ priya
english: "Where have you gone, O gambler, cutting off half my garment, abandoning in the forest your beloved and devoted one who lay asleep, O beloved?"

sanskrit: sā vai yathā samādiṣṭā tatrāste tvatpratīkṣiṇī dahyamānā bhṛśaṃ bālā vastrārdhenābhisaṃvṛtā
english: "As commanded by you, she waits there for you, that young woman, burning greatly with longing, wrapped in half a garment."

sanskrit: tasyā rudantyāḥ satataṃ tena śokena pārthiva prasādaṃ kuru vai vīra prativākyaṃ dadasva ca
english: "For her who weeps ceaselessly with that grief, O lord of the earth, show grace, O hero, and give a word in reply."

sanskrit: etad anyac ca vaktavyaṃ kṛpāṃ kuryād yathā mayi vāyunā dhūyamāno hi vanaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ
english: "This and something else is to be said — that he may show compassion to me; for fire fanned by wind burns the forest."

sanskrit: bhartavyā rakṣaṇīyā ca patnī hi patinā sadā tan naṣṭam ubhayaṃ kasmād dharmajñasya satas tava
english: "A wife must always be maintained and protected by her husband — why have both these duties been abandoned by you, who are righteous and good?"

sanskrit: khyātaḥ prājñaḥ kulīnaś ca sānukrośaś ca tvaṃ sadā saṃvṛtto niranukrośaḥ śaṅke madbhāgyasaṃkṣayāt
english: "You are renowned, wise, well-born, and always compassionate; now you are transformed to mercilessness — I think it is because of the destruction of my fortune."

sanskrit: sa kuruṣva maheṣvāsa dayāṃ mayi nararṣabha ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharmas tvatta eva hi me śrutam
english: "Therefore show compassion to me, O great archer, O bull among men; non-cruelty is the highest virtue — this very teaching I heard from you."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇān yadi vaḥ pratibrūyād dhi kaś cana sa naraḥ sarvathā jñeyaḥ kaś cāsau kva ca vartate
english: "If, while you speak thus, any man responds to you, that man is to be fully identified — who he is and where he dwells."

sanskrit: yac ca vo vacanaṃ śrutvā brūyāt prativaco naraḥ tad ādāya vacaḥ kṣipraṃ mamāvedyaṃ dvijottamāḥ
english: "Whatever answer a man gives upon hearing your words, bring back that speech and report it to me swiftly, O best of twice-born."

sanskrit: yathā ca vo na jānīyāc carato bhīmaśāsanāt punarāgamanaṃ caiva tathā kāryam atandritaiḥ
english: "And act with diligence so that he may not know you are wandering by Bhīma's command and that you will be returning."

sanskrit: yadi vāsau samṛddhaḥ syād yadi vāpy adhano bhavet yadi vāpy arthakāmaḥ syāj jñeyam asya cikīrṣitam
english: "Whether he be prosperous, or whether he be without wealth, or whether he desire riches — his intentions are to be discerned."

sanskrit: evam uktās tv agacchaṃs te brāhmaṇāḥ sarvatodiśam nalaṃ mṛgayituṃ rājaṃs tathā vyasaninaṃ tadā
english: Thus instructed, those brahmins set out in all directions, O king, to search for Nala who was then afflicted with adversity.

sanskrit: te purāṇi sarāṣṭrāṇi grāmān ghoṣāṃs tathāśramān anveṣanto nalaṃ rājan nādhijagmur dvijātayaḥ
english: Those twice-born ones searched cities with their kingdoms, villages, cow-herding settlements, and hermitages, O king, but did not find Nala.

sanskrit: tac ca vākyaṃ tathā sarve tatra tatra viśāṃ pate śrāvayāṃ cakrire viprā damayantyā yatheritam
english: And all those brahmins, O lord of people, proclaimed that message here and there, everywhere, exactly as Damayantī had directed.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca atha dīrghasya kālasya parṇādo nāma vai dvijaḥ pratyetya nagaraṃ bhaimīm idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Then, after a long time, a brahmin named Parṇāda returned to the city and spoke these words to the daughter of Bhīma:

sanskrit: naiṣadhaṃ mṛgayānena damayanti divāniśam ayodhyāṃ nagarīṃ gatvā bhāṅgasvarir upasthitaḥ
english: "Searching day and night for the lord of Niṣadha, O Damayantī, I went to the city of Ayodhyā and presented myself before Bhāṅgasvari (Ṛtuparṇa)."

sanskrit: śrāvitaś ca mayā vākyaṃ tvadīyaṃ sa mahājane ṛtuparṇo mahābhāgo yathoktaṃ varavarṇini
english: "And I caused that greatly blessed Ṛtuparṇa to hear your message in a great assembly, exactly as it was spoken, O fair-complexioned one."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā nābravīt kiṃ cid ṛtuparṇo narādhipaḥ na ca pāriṣadaḥ kaś cid bhāṣyamāṇo mayāsakṛt
english: "Hearing that, Ṛtuparṇa, the lord of men, said nothing; nor did any member of his court speak, even as I proclaimed it repeatedly."

sanskrit: anujñātaṃ tu māṃ rājñā vijane kaś cid abravīt ṛtuparṇasya puruṣo bāhuko nāma nāmataḥ
english: "But when I was dismissed by the king, someone spoke to me in a private place — a servant of Ṛtuparṇa named Bāhuka."

sanskrit: sūtas tasya narendrasya virūpo hrasvabāhukaḥ śīghrayāne sukuśalo mṛṣṭakartā ca bhojane
english: "He is the charioteer of that lord of men, misshapen in form and with short arms — Bāhuka is his name; he is supremely skilled in swift driving and also a fine preparer of food."

sanskrit: sa viniḥśvasya bahuśo ruditvā ca muhur muhuḥ kuśalaṃ caiva māṃ pṛṣṭvā paścād idam abhāṣata
english: "He sighed deeply many times and wept again and again; having inquired after your welfare, he then spoke these words:"

sanskrit: vaiṣamyam api saṃprāptā gopāyanti kulastriyaḥ ātmānam ātmanā satyo jitasvargā na saṃśayaḥ rahitā bhartṛbhiś caiva na krudhyanti kadā cana
english: "'Women of good family, even when fallen into adversity, protect themselves by their own virtue; those who are true and have won heaven — of that there is no doubt — never become angry, even when abandoned by their husbands.'"

sanskrit: viṣamasthena mūḍhena paribhraṣṭasukhena ca yat sā tena parityaktā tatra na kroddhum arhati
english: "'She who was abandoned by one placed in adversity, by one confused, by one fallen from happiness — in that she ought not to be angry with him.'"

sanskrit: prāṇayātrāṃ pariprepsoḥ śakunair hṛtavāsasaḥ ādhibhir dahyamānasya śyāmā na kroddhum arhati
english: "'At one who was struggling to sustain his very life, whose garments were stolen by birds, who was burning with anguish — the dark-complexioned one ought not to be angry.'"

sanskrit: satkṛtāsatkṛtā vāpi patiṃ dṛṣṭvā tathāgatam bhraṣṭarājyaṃ śriyā hīnaṃ śyāmā na kroddhum arhati
english: "'Whether honored or dishonored, upon seeing her husband who has come to such a pass — fallen from his kingdom, bereft of prosperity — the dark-complexioned one ought not to be angry.'"

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā tvarito 'ham ihāgataḥ śrutvā pramāṇaṃ bhavatī rājñaś caiva nivedaya
english: "Having heard his words, I have come here in haste; having heard, O noble lady, you must weigh this evidence and also inform the king."
